# Independent audit of the defect cap-load inequality and quadratic reserve

Source read in full: `candidate 3432196fb93eb580`.


## 1. The remainder is genuinely pointwise controlled

The required estimate |R_j|<=C lambda_j follows from the actual nonregular multicontact density in `candidate 1a7cfa3d1047cbae`, not just from convergence of its surface L1 norm. Uniform source inballs give a positive lower ordinary energy; its optimal projective denominator has the uniform floor 1/(d+1). Summing the nonnegative energy coefficients costs at most a fixed multiple of Delta_j. The continuous cap normals are bounded under the positive covariance normalization, the body diameters are bounded, and the covariance correction has total coefficient Delta_j. The remaining constant is also a fixed multiple of Delta_j. Since M_j is bounded above and below and lambda_j=Delta_j/[(d+1)M_j], all these terms are bounded by C lambda_j at every old regular boundary point.

This matters: the tests grow in the logarithmic layer, so surface L1 convergence alone would not justify their use. Here their integral is controlled by the unscaled uniform logarithmic trace bound.

## 2. Defect extraction retains the actual allocations

The measures (-log L_j)_+ eta_j and W_j(-log L_j)_+ eta_j are uniformly bounded and ordered. Uniform convergence of L_j identifies their restrictions off Z={L=0}. The ordinary limiting negative logarithm is integrable by truncation. Since eta(Z)=0, their residual restrictions to Z are nonnegative and satisfy 0<=a<=b. Thus a is a limit of the SAME prelimit cap loads, not a newly chosen cap indicator on the zero faces.

The bound for q_j=lambda_j(-log L_j)_+^2 eta_j follows from the admissible test (-log L_j-1)_+ and the exact inequality s^2<=s(s-1)_++s. The selected beta_j are normalized depths in [0,1]; this supplies the printed constant 1 in the upper bound. In an abstract version with merely bounded beta_j it can be replaced by a fixed bound on their positive parts. No additional assumption is needed in the stated application. The reserve q is supported on Z because lambda_j tends to zero and the logarithms are locally bounded off Z.

## 3. Convexity and actual global extension

The Hessian of a log(a/b) is

    [[1/a,-1/b],[-1/b,a/b^2]],

which is positive semidefinite with determinant zero for a,b>0. Subtracting T a and taking the maximum with zero preserves joint convexity. On its positive branch, the a derivative is log(a/b)-T+1>1 and the b derivative is -a/b<0; on its zero branch the function is constant. Therefore composition with positive convex f and positive concave L_j is convex.

For each fixed j, L_j and f are positive on a convex thickening of the current canonical compact hull. The composed function has bounded subgradients on a smaller such thickening. The supremum of those supporting affine functions is globally finite and convex and agrees on the current hull. This is an actual admissible test, despite its j-dependent slope bound. The source does not need a uniform global Lipschitz bound or a fixed test independent of j: the same separator has already been obtained for all such tests at each j.

## 4. The limit order and reserve coefficient

For fixed T>sup log f, write c=T-log f>0. The identity

    f(ell_j-c)_+=f ell_(j,+)-f min(ell_(j,+),c)

separates an actual weighted defect measure from a bounded continuous weak-limit test. It gives the printed ordinary-tail term plus f(a-beta b), with no missing threshold constant on the defect. The logarithmic correction satisfies pointwise

    |lambda_j ell_j f(ell_j-c)_+
                       -f lambda_j ell_(j,+)^2|
       <=lambda_j f c ell_(j,+).

The right integral tends to zero at each fixed T. Therefore the reserve has coefficient exactly one. The other correction is bounded by C lambda_j integral ell_(j,+) and also tends to zero. Only after this j limit is T sent to infinity; the ordinary boundary tail then vanishes by dominated convergence. Finally f+delta gives all nonnegative convex tests.

The resulting inequality is precisely

    integral psi(n) f(w) d(a+q)
       <=beta integral psi(n) f(w) db

for nonnegative continuous normal tests psi and nonnegative globally finite convex physical f. Its mass deficit must be retained; signed affine moment equality is not implied.

## 5. Connection and scope

The independent flux theorem `candidate d9362f528596f345` supplies the vector and positive radial relation between b and the tilted-volume defects. The present theorem adds cap-load information using the same prelimit physical separator. Neither result identifies the boundary-cap coupling with the volume rows, excludes their defects, or proves a numerical depth bound.

The exact checker `supporting computation verify_logarithmic_defect_tail_audit_slab_recovery.py` verifies the Hessian, perspective derivatives, and both scalar inequalities on a rational grid including their seams. Those checks support the elementary algebra; the normal-bundle convergence and two-limit argument are audited analytically above.
